title: Rider Premium Charges, Payments and Credits on the Premium Account
content:
Standing instruction of the premium accounting desk on entries posted to the premium account of any of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders.

## 1. The charging clause, no longer in force

The clause "The rider premium is charged for each coverage month from the rider effective date to the rider end date, and on the tiers that bill it with the plan it appears as its own line on the medical plan bill" is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis on which the coverage months one rider premium charge carries are settled. The rate each rider carries, the day its premium falls due and whether it is carried on the medical plan bill remain the terms of the rider held and are unaffected by that retirement.

## 2. When an entry may be posted

The rider stands in its waiting period, active or suspended for unpaid premium on the day the charge is posted. The standing is read from the rider's own record — its reference, its standing and the day it took effect — before the charge, the payment or the credit is posted, and it is that rider's record, named by its own reference, that governs.

## 3. No payment posted twice

No payment entry carrying the same remittance reference and the same amount is already posted on this rider. This is judged before the payment is posted, on the rider's own premium account entries: their references, the remittance reference each carries, the amount each carries and what kind of entry each is. Two payment entries that differ in the day they were posted or in the coverage month they are booked to are separate entries rather than one repeated.

## 4. Premium during the waiting period

Premium is owed during the waiting period, because the rider is in force even though it is not yet paying, and a member surprised by that is shown the two dates on their record.

## 5. The order money is applied in

Money is posted against the oldest unpaid coverage month first, and a payment that covers both the plan premium and the rider premium is split between them in that order.

## 6. Credits

A credit always names the single rider premium charge it relieves and the reason, and never exceeds that charge; a rider cancelled part way through a month is credited in whole months only.

## 7. Coverage months beyond the rider end date

No rider premium is charged for a coverage month beginning after the rider end date, and a charge already posted for such a month is relieved by a credit rather than chased.

## Points of judgement

**A suspended rider is still open for entries.** A rider suspended for unpaid premium is one of the three standings on which a charge, a payment or a credit may be posted; a rider that has ended is not.

**The plan premium is met first out of a combined payment.** Where one payment covers both the medical plan premium and the rider premium, it is split between them in that order.

**A credit is bounded by the charge it names.** A credit never exceeds the single rider premium charge it relieves.

superseded_clauses: The rider premium is charged for each coverage month from the rider effective date to the rider end date, and on the tiers that bill it with the plan it appears as its own line on the medical plan bill.
